extracted.intended_audience: NIH applicants, grantees, institutional signing officials (SO), account administrators (AA), principal investigators (PIs), referees, and grantor agency/staff who use eRA Commons
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and requirements for using the eRA Commons web system to register organizations, manage accounts and roles, submit and track grant applications and post-award reports (RPPR, FFR, JIT, RAM, etc.), and submit reference letters. Covers system-specific file/format constraints, role responsibilities, authentication, and submission workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment file format and size
rubrics_metrics.description: All attachments should be submitted in PDF format with a maximum size of 6MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure uploaded attachments are PDF and do not exceed 6MB; use PDF flattening where required (see Flattening PDFs for Application Submission and Commons). The system's upload areas indicate allowed file types and counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letter format and content constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for reference letters: 'No longer than two pages; Not password-protected; In flattened PDF format. The PDF should not be a fillable form PDF (it should be flattened).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Fellowship and Career Development programs, a Letter of Reference form is no longer required — a letter on university letterhead or similar is acceptable. Check your PDF is flattened and not password-protected before upload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where and when reference letters are accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference letters can be submitted any time after the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) is posted and no later than the submission deadline, and reference letters cannot be accepted through any means other than eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees do not need to log in to eRA Commons to submit; however, the candidate must have a valid Commons account with the PI role. If the candidate lacks that role/account, the referee will receive an error when attempting submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letter submission prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting a reference letter you need: Applicant's Commons User ID, Applicant's last name as it appears on the Commons account, Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) number, and the deadline for submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If replacing a previously-submitted letter, you also need the confirmation number from the original submission. The applicant should provide the necessary identifiers and deadline to the referee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letter replacement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: You may replace a previously submitted reference letter only if the application deadline has not passed and you know the confirmation number from the first submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To replace, follow the same submission steps and enter the original submission confirmation number in the Reference Letter Confirmation # field. Keep the confirmation number emailed to you after initial submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission confirmation and visibility for referees and applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: After submitting a reference letter, a message appears showing a confirmation number and you receive an email with the confirmation number. The candidate receives a confirmation email that the letter was submitted but cannot see the reference letter you've submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the confirmation number; it's required to replace the letter if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization registration requirement and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization is required to register in eRA Commons to electronically submit a grant application. The organization must be registered by a person who has signature authority to legally bind the organization in grants administration matters, referred to as a signing official (SO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only authorized organization officials can be deemed SOs; examples include Corporation - President/CEO, Institute - Executive Director, University - President/Dean/Chancellor. During registration, accounts for the signing official (SO) and account administrator (AA) are created.

rubrics_metrics.name: First accounts created during registration
rubrics_metrics.description: During registration, accounts for the signing official (SO) and account administrator (AA) are created. The first signing official can create additional signing official accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After registration becomes active, SO and AA can create new user accounts for personnel and access Institution Profile information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications due on or after January 25, 2022, applicants must have a UEI at the time of application submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The UEI replaces the DUNS number and is obtained from SAM.gov. Update institutional profile and registration processes to use UEI instead of DUNS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role-based access and functions in Commons
rubrics_metrics.description: Users are assigned specific roles (e.g., PI, SO, AA, AO, ASST, BO, FCOI, SPONSOR) and, depending on role, can perform a variety of functions in Commons such as tracking submission status, viewing summary statements, viewing Notice of Award, submitting JIT, submitting FFR/Final RPPR, no-cost extensions, and managing profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the privileges and responsibilities of each role; some searches and actions require specific roles (e.g., SO role for certain Status searches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-factor authentication requirement for certain users
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal investigators, reviewers, and key personnel associated with an application or an RPPR are required to use two factor authentication for enhanced security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-factor can be provided through a federated (organization) account if it meets NIH-required security requirements, or through Login.gov. If required to transition, users will receive a message upon login guiding them through using Login.gov with eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Login methods supported
rubrics_metrics.description: There are four login methods in the login section to access eRA Commons: Login.gov, eRA Credentials, Federated (InCommon) Account, and PIV/CAC smartcard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate method for your account type; organizations transitioning to federated access must meet NIH security requirements to be used for two-factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: RAM (Request for Additional Materials) constraints and behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: There can only be one active (i.e. non-submitted) RAM request at a time to which changes can be made by any authorized user. Once submitted, a new RAM is required for additional changes. There is no limit to the number of RAMs a user can submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both PI and SO can edit the RAM while active. The system provides an audit trail of who uploaded documents. Click Preview to see a consolidated PDF of all uploaded documents (latest on top). When the RAM is submitted, an email notification is sent to the government project officer (GPO), grant technical assistant (GTA), and grants management specialist (GMS).

rubrics_metrics.name: File upload interactions and workflow (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: When uploading files (RAM, reference letters, etc.), users may drag and drop files or browse. For uploaded files, you may click the Download icon to open/download the file or click the Delete icon to remove it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The drop area indicates allowed file types and how many files are allowed. Use Preview to view a combined PDF prior to submission. 'Save' keeps the upload without submitting; 'Submit' sends to the agency. Tip: Check all documents after uploading to ensure correct files are submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letter submission technical restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference letter PDFs must not be password-protected and must be flattened (not fillable forms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the PDF is flattened and openable before uploading. The system will reject or cause problems for password-protected or form-type PDFs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for referees about candidate account status
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the referee does not need a Commons role or to log in, the candidate must have a valid Commons account and hold the principal investigator (PI) role; otherwise referees receive an error when attempting to submit a letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidate's SO, AA, or AO must assign the PI role to the candidate's Commons account prior to referee submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search actions requiring role and login
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain searches (e.g., Finding Recent NoAs, Awards with RPPRs Due, or Awards Pending Closeout) require that the user be logged into eRA Commons and have the signing official (SO) role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These searches replace Quick Queries and are performed via the Status or RPPR modules; follow module-specific steps to filter results (e.g., Closeout status, Not Started RPPRs).
